title: Adam Hamilton continues bus tour with stops in Topeka, Independence, and Pittsburg
text:
Adam Hamilton continues bus tour with stops in Topeka, Independence, and Pittsburg
Adam Hamilton continued his Leading from the Middle bus tour with stops in Topeka, Independence, and Pittsburg. Hamilton met with Kansans to discuss economic concerns, bipartisanship, and his Senate campaign priorities.
October 29, Adam Hamilton continued his Leading from the Middle bus tour with stops in Topeka, Independence, and Pittsburg. After casting his vote in Overland Park, Hamilton traveled across Kansas to meet with residents concerned about rising prices and seeking a Senator who will address their needs.
Hamilton’s first stop was at Washburn University in Topeka, where he listened to students discuss their concerns about economic pressures and their futures. He spoke about his commitment to bipartisanship and pledged to work with anyone in Washington to create opportunities for young Kansans. In Independence, Hamilton addressed a crowd that included Democrats, Republicans, and Independents, sharing his plans to prioritize Kansas over party politics.
The day concluded in Pittsburg, where Hamilton met with voters at Chicken Mary’s, a local restaurant. “All across Kansas, people are saying we’ve got to work together to lower costs, stop the chaos and corruption in Washington, and fix our broken politics. Roger Marshall has spent a decade in Washington ignoring the needs of Kansans. Kansans are tired of being left behind by Washington politicians, and we’re ready for an independent-minded Senator who will stand up for Kansas,” said Adam Hamilton.
Hamilton, a fifth-generation Kansan, has served as pastor of a congregation made up of Republicans, Democrats, and Independents. The congregation has contributed hundreds of thousands of volunteer hours and raised tens of millions of dollars to support local communities, according to Hamilton. He has been married to his high school sweetheart, LaVon, for 44 years and has two daughters, a granddaughter, and two dogs.
Hamilton said he is running for Senate to lower costs, protect health care for Kansans, and address what he describes as chaos and corruption in Washington.
